items.claim: The span's rationale states that the 'he said to me' sweep does not begin until chapter 8. Eight verses of that 36-verse sweep stand inside MT 2:1-3:24, at MT 2:1, MT 2:3, MT 3:1, MT 3:3, MT 3:4, MT 3:10, MT 3:22 and MT 3:24. The same paragraph then names the 'he said to me' at MT 2:1 as the device marking the far side of this unit's own close, so the sentence contradicts itself on the bytes and on the corpus. The narrower statement the span actually needs holds: over MT 1:4-1:27 the counts are word-event 0, messenger 0, utterance 0, recognition 0, 'he said to me' 0, transport 0, parashah marks 0.
items.both_sides: Onset side MT 1:1-1:3: two datelines in two counting systems at MT 1:1 and MT 1:2 (2 of the 14 dateline verses), the third-person word-event at MT 1:3, and the hand-of-YHWH construct in that same verse (1 of the 7 carrying it). Close side MT 1:28: the glory sighting, the prophet falling on his face and hearing a voice, with a samekh on that verse; across the seam MT 2:1 turns to direct address with 'he said to me' and the son-of-man address. Between the two, MT 1:4-1:27 carries no formula verse of any class and no parashah mark (24 verses swept, 0 hits in each class), so the 28-verse span holds one movement and the seam at MT 1:28/2:1 is evidenced on both sides. The low confidence is right for a span at roughly four times the book's typical row density.

suggested_fix.fact: scope the absence claim to the span itself - 0 'he said to me' verses fall inside MT 1:4-1:27 - and drop the extension of it to the book before chapter 8, which eight verses in MT 2:1-3:24 contradict

items.claim: MT 2:3 opens with the same 'he said to me' plus son-of-man pair on which this unit's own onset at MT 2:1 rests, and a pe is recorded on MT 2:2 directly before it. The strongest internal seam candidate in the span therefore carries a device on its onset side and a mark on its close side. The row discloses the mark at MT 2:2 as sub-paragraph texture and does not disclose the device at MT 2:3 by role at all, although the book's own discipline requires a row to state the formula devices its span carries as onset, sub-onset or close.
items.both_sides: Close side of the 2:2/2:3 candidate: MT 2:2 has the Spirit set the prophet on his feet and the prophet hear the speaker - a completed action with a pe on the verse, but no refrain and no signature, so the near side offers no refrain-grade close. Onset side MT 2:3: 'he said to me', the son-of-man address and the sending itself. A cut there leaves MT 2:1-2:2 at two verses, under the size floor, with no word-event and no close formula, while MT 2:3-2:7 carries the unit's burden and closes on the hear-or-refuse pair with a pe on MT 2:7. The 7-verse span stands, and the seam behind it at MT 1:28 is itself samekh-marked.

suggested_fix.fact: disclose the 'he said to me' plus son-of-man address at MT 2:3 by role, as a sub-onset weighed and not cut, beside the pe already disclosed on the verse before it

items.claim: MT 2:8-3:3 holds one literary movement - the command to open the mouth and eat, the scroll stretched out and read, the eating and its sweetness - opened by the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset at MT 2:8 directly after a pe-marked close at MT 2:7 and closed at MT 3:3 where a pe is recorded. The samekh on MT 2:10 falls inside the movement and the row discloses it without cutting on it, and the translation's chapter division at 2:10/3:1 is named only as tier-4 texture and refused as boundary evidence. Both disclosures are correct against the witness.
items.both_sides: Onset side MT 2:8: the address turns from the audience's character to the prophet's own act, with the rebellious-house naming (3rd of the 6 in MT 2:1-3:27) and the imperative to eat; behind it MT 2:7 closes on the hear-or-refuse pair with a pe on the verse. Close side MT 3:3: the scroll is eaten and tastes of honey, with a pe on that verse; across the seam MT 3:4 turns from the scroll to the errand with a fresh 'he said to me' and the son-of-man address. The scene runs across the chapter numeral without a formula break: the 'he said to me' verses at MT 3:1 and MT 3:3 continue the same scroll scene rather than opening new ones, and no mark stands at the numeral itself.

items.claim: Two statements in the row's prose do not hold against the bytes. First, MT 3:9 is the fourth of the six verses in MT 2:1-3:27 that name the rebellious house (MT 2:5, 2:6, 2:8, 3:9, 3:26, 3:27), and the row calls it the third; the fifth and sixth of that same series are counted correctly elsewhere in this cluster, so the series is internally inconsistent by one. Second, the rejected alternative asserts that no onset device distinguishes MT 3:10-3:11, while MT 3:10 carries the 'he said to me' plus son-of-man pair that the row's own onset at MT 3:4 rests on, with a rebellious-house naming and a pe on MT 3:9 immediately before it; the sweep the row does run tests only for a word-event, a hand-of-YHWH construct and a dateline, a test it did not apply to its own onset.
items.both_sides: Close side of the 3:9/3:10 candidate: MT 3:9 ends on the rebellious-house naming, refrain-grade close evidence, with a pe on the verse. Onset side: MT 3:10 opens with 'he said to me' and the son-of-man address, and MT 3:11 turns the errand from the house of Israel, addressed through MT 3:4-3:9, to the exiles and the children of your people, an addressee change, closing on the messenger formula and the hear-or-refuse pair. The seam is therefore real on both sides, and the span still stands: a cut leaves MT 3:10-3:11 at two verses, under the size floor, with 0 of the 49 any-form word-event verses, 0 of the 7 hand-of-YHWH verses and 0 of the 14 dateline verses falling in it, and the same commission speech runs across it into the transport at MT 3:12. What must change is the ground, not the span.

suggested_fix.fact: correct the ordinal - MT 3:9 is the fourth of the six rebellious-house verses in MT 2:1-3:27 - and replace the flat denial with the weighed statement that MT 3:10 carries the 'he said to me' plus son-of-man pair and MT 3:11 the addressee change to the exiles, the seam being declined on the two-verse size floor and the shared errand rather than on an absence of devices

items.claim: MT 3:12-3:15 holds one movement, the return journey from the vision to the exiles: lifted by the Spirit at MT 3:12, carried away in bitterness at MT 3:14, arriving at Tel Aviv and sitting seven days at MT 3:15. The hand-of-YHWH construct at MT 3:14 is weighed and refused as an onset because no scene change accompanies it, which is the reading the book's own use supports against the two verses in this parent where the construct does open a scene, MT 1:3 and MT 3:22. The absence of a parashah mark on MT 3:15 is disclosed and is correctly not treated as counterevidence.
items.both_sides: Onset side MT 3:12: narrated action with no address and no imperative, set against the commission speech that ends at MT 3:11 on the messenger formula and the hear-or-refuse pair. Close side MT 3:15: the seven days of sitting, a report rather than a refrain, with no mark on the verse - of the 11 verses in MT chapters 1-3 that carry a parashah mark, MT 3:15 is not one. Across the seam MT 3:16 answers those same seven days and carries the strict word-event form, a hard seam. The four-verse span is short but complete, and its close is fixed by the onset that follows rather than by a device of its own, which is what the medium_low confidence records.

suggested_fix.fact: no change to the span or the confidence; the transit reading of the hand-of-YHWH construct is what the surrounding narrative carries, and the unmarked close is disclosed rather than argued around

items.claim: The pe is recorded on MT 3:16, the verse whose first clause is the seven-days notice and whose second is the strict word-event. The unsourceable question is therefore whether the mark stands inside MT 3:16, between those two clauses, or after that verse, and that is precisely what decides whether the mark corroborates the seam at MT 3:15/3:16. The row instead frames the open question as whether the mark falls before or after the watchman charge at MT 3:17, which the witness does not leave open: a mark recorded on MT 3:16 cannot stand beyond MT 3:17. The disclosure is stated on the wrong verse and so gives away an argument the row's own onset could have used.
items.both_sides: Onset side MT 3:16: the strict word-event form, a hard seam no unit crosses, with the pe recorded on that verse and not on MT 3:15 - the mark's placement on the onset verse is itself evidence about where the seam falls. Close side MT 3:15: the arrival and the seven days of sitting, narrative, with no mark. Inside the span the samekh on MT 3:19 separates the wicked-man case from the righteous-man case and both are one paired illustration of the single charge at MT 3:17, with no onset device standing at MT 3:20; the samekh on MT 3:21 closes the unit before the hand-of-YHWH construct reopens the scene at MT 3:22. The span and its medium confidence stand; only the disclosure needs relocating.

suggested_fix.fact: state the unsettled placement on the verse that carries the mark - whether the pe stands inside MT 3:16, between the seven-days clause and the word-event clause, or after that verse - instead of on the watchman charge

items.claim: MT 3:22-3:27 is opened by the hand-of-YHWH construct at MT 3:22, one of the two uses in this parent that do open a scene, and closed at MT 3:27 by the sixth and last rebellious-house naming in MT 2:1-3:27 with a samekh on that verse. The seam at MT 3:27/4:1 is argued from both sides, with the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset at MT 4:1 on the far side, and the rope word shared by MT 3:25 and MT 4:8 is disclosed as continuity against the row's own seam rather than suppressed. The ordinal series the row states is the one the bytes carry, and the alternative parent boundary at MT 3:15/3:16 is weighed from both sides and held rather than argued away.
items.both_sides: Close side MT 3:27: the promise that the mouth will be opened, the hear-or-refuse pair and the rebellious-house naming - refrain-grade close - with a samekh on the verse. Onset side MT 4:1: 'and you, son of man' with the imperative to take a tile, the sub-onset that starts the sign-act series, with a samekh on MT 4:3 closing the first of those acts. The single device arguing continuity across the seam is the rope word, standing at MT 3:25 and again at MT 4:8, identical once accents are set aside (sweep of the pointed form over the staged MT extract: 3 verses, MT 3:25, MT 4:8 and MT 31:10, the last in another sense); the row discloses it as continuity and the seam still stands on the refrain, the mark and the sub-onset. On the held alternative, the pe stands on MT 3:16 rather than on MT 3:15, which the row states correctly and which weighs against a parent boundary at 3:15/3:16 without closing the question.

suggested_fix.fact: no change; the onset device, the refrain close and its mark, the disclosed continuity device and the held alternative are each anchored on the verse that carries them, and the operative-category deviation for the muteness charge inside a vision-opened scene is disclosed

e19_selfreport: I ran no listing, no glob and no recursive search - not against my output directory, not against the worktree, and not against my own scratch. Every file I opened was named by exact path in my brief, in my launch message, in the governance set my own global policy requires, or in the ledger my launch message named, and each pinned input was hashed by exact path before I read it; all thirteen digests matched the brief's table. No directory was tested for existence, no wildcard or glob parameter was used in any tool call, and I created no private scratch files - the intermediate sweeps ran in memory and printed to the transcript. The deliverable was written directly to the exact path my launch message names.
